FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 February 1985, after the draft finalized by the Dye Intermediates Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council.

0.2 Sulphotobias acid ( C!~eI-IsOsNSz ) is an important dye intermediate for the manufacture of coal tar dyestuffs. It is also known as 2-naphthylamine-1: 5-disulphonic acid. It is available in the form of its monosodium salt. It is represented by the following structural formula:
SO,H I

A-0.l Dry the material at 105 & 1�C to constant mass. Grind and the material to a wide-mouthed bottle and stopper mix well. Transfer it. Do not expose the sample to an atmosphere containing acidic or alkaline fumes. Use this prepared sample for tests. A-l. ASSAY ( BY NITRITE VALUE ) A-l.0 Outline of the Method - The material is dissolved in aqueous sodium hydroxide. A known volume of the solution is titrated in acidic medium with standard sodium nitrite solution, using starch-iodide test paper as an external indicator.

A-1.1.4 Starch-Iodide Test Papers
A-1.2

Procedure

A-1.2.1 Weigh accurately 15 to 20 g of the prepared sample in previously weighed dry weighing bottle with stopper. Transfer it to 500-ml volumetric flask with a jet of water from wash bottle, Add small quantities of sodium hydroxide at a time till the sample dissolves. Dilute the solution with water up to the mark. Stopper the flask and shake well. A-1.2.2 Take 50 ml of this solution in a one-litre beaker. Add 400 ml of distilled water, 30 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid, and ice to Then add 3 g potassium bromide cool the solution between 0 to 5�C. End and titrate against standard sodium nitrite solution from burette. point of blue ring is developed on starch iodide paper with a drop of solution from beaker. Confirm development of blue ring on starch iodide with a drop of solution from beaker without further addition of sodium nitrite solution. Note the reading of standard sodium nitrite solution consumed. A-1.2.3 Repeat the above experiment and note the reading of standard sodium nitrite consumed. The two readings of standard sodium nitrite solution consumed should not differ by more than 0.1 ml. A-2.4.1 Place 200 ml of developing solvent mixture ( A-2.1.10 ) into the tank and replace the lid. Allow to equilibriate for about an hour. A-2.5 Development of Chromatogram A-2.5.1 After spotting, suspend the paper from the supporting rods by means of clips so that a lower edge of the paper is just touching the surface of the developing solvent but not stood on the bottom of the tank. Allow the chromatogram to develop for about 16 hours. After developing and drying at 65"C, develop fluorescence by holding the When paper over a beaker containing concentrated ammonia solution. the paper examined under an ultra violet lamp the folkWing zones are seen: i) The main band 2-naphthylamine-1,5 disulphonic blue fluorescence is seen at the bottom; and ii) Pinkish blue fluorescence A-2.5.2 under: Further assessment shall be made acid of strong .`, of tobias acid is seen at the top. by coupling `method as

IS : -11181 - lM5 A-3.2 Procedure

A-3.2.1 Weigh accurately about 15 g of the prepdred sample (see A-0.1) and transfer to a 500-ml beaker. Paste well with about 100 ml of water. Add sodium carbonate solution till alkaline to brilliant yellow indicator paper. Add about 200 ml of water and heat to dissolve the material completely. Filter hot through counter-poised Whatman filter paper. Wash the residue with hot water till the washings are free from alkali. Dry the residue at 100 f 5�C to constant mass. A-3.2.2 Transfer quantitatively the filtrate and washings together into a 500-ml volumetric flask and dilute with water up to the mark at room temperature. Mix well. IS :11181-1985 A-4.3 Procedure

A-4.3.1 Weigh accurately about 20 g of prepared sample ( see A-0.1 ) and transfer quantitatively into 800-ml beaker, add 400 ml water. Warm and add 1 M sodium carbonate until the solution is just alkaline to brilliant yellow paper. Filter and wash with hot .water until the Cool the washings are no longer ~alkaline to brilliant yellow paper. filtrate and washings and transfer quantitatively to a 1-litre measuring flask, dilute to the mark with water and mix well. Pipette loo-ml of the solution into a 500-ml airtight glass stoppered narrow necked bottle, add 5.2 ml of 1N sulphuric acid and 25 ml of N/10 iodine solution followed by 20 ml sodium acetate solution ( A-4.1.4 ). Stopper the bottle, shake, and allow to stand overnight in a dark cupboard.

A-4.3.2 Remove the bottle from the cupboard, add 20 ml glacial acetic acid, wash the stopper with the acetic acid, add 100 ml water, Titrate with N/10 sodium mix and allow to stand for 5 minutes. thiosulphate, using starch solution as indicator towards the end of the Carry out a blank test using 100 ml~water instead of 100 ml titration. test solution.
